title: Squirrel Simulation
summary: Given a garden of dimensions height x width, along with the positions of a tree, a squirrel, and multiple nuts, determine the minimal distance the squirrel must travel to collect all the nuts and place them under the tree one by one.
statement: Given a garden of dimensions height x width, along with the positions of a tree, a squirrel, and multiple nuts, determine the minimal distance the squirrel must travel to collect all the nuts and place them under the tree one by one. The squirrel can move one cell at a time in any of the four cardinal directions: up, down, left, and right.
constraints: All positions lie in the garden; moves are orthogonal with Manhattan distance.
hints: Except for the first nut, each nut requires a tree-to-nut-to-tree trip.
Start from all round trips, then choose the nut with the greatest first-trip saving.
Compute 2*tree-distance for every nut; subtract max(tree-distance minus squirrel-distance).
Only the first carried nut changes the usual round-trip route, so the choices are independent.
editorial: Only the first carried nut changes the usual round-trip route, so the choices are independent.

tests.explanation: A round trip from tree for each nut costs 14; starting with the best nut saves two, for 12.
The squirrel starts on the only nut, so it needs only the trip from nut to tree.
